analysis.summary: The tRPC client is misconfigured to access both public and private routers through a single endpoint, but the backend now serves them on separate URLs, causing all private procedure calls to fail at runtime.

bugs.title: tRPC client cannot access private routes
bugs.description: The client is created with a single URL endpoint (`${baseUrl}/bff`) but the type signature claims to support both AppRouter and PrivateRouter procedures. However, the backend infrastructure changes moved private routes to a separate URL path (`${privateBaseUrl}/bff`) served by a different handler. When the client attempts to call private procedures (postCart, deleteCart, etc.), it will send requests to the public endpoint which does not have those procedures registered, resulting in 'procedure not found' errors.
bugs.risk: All cart mutation operations (postCart, deleteCart, postEntry, deleteEntry, replaceEntry) and compatibility checks will fail at runtime because the client sends them to the wrong HTTP endpoint.

notBugs.reason: Intentional architectural change to separate public read-only operations from private write operations. The split itself is correct; the issue is only in the client configuration that fails to account for the separate endpoints.

notBugs.topic: Removal of pathRewrite in webpack dev server
notBugs.reason: This aligns the development environment with the new production routing where API Gateway handles the full path including the base URL prefix. The change is consistent with the BffApi.ts route definitions.
The URL rewriting logic is no longer needed because the API Gateway routes in BffApi.ts now explicitly include the full path patterns (`/__app__/...` and `/__app-private__/...`).
